title: Fractional safety pool, noise-detection and graceful rebalance for dedicated GPUs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated pools occasionally experience noisy-neighbor events where a single tenant's bursty workload (long context generation or huge batch) causes other tenants' tail latency and throughput to degrade. Existing hard-slicing approaches reduce utilization; pure best-effort sharing causes unpredictability for SLAs.

Proposal: Implement a fractional safety pool combined with real-time noise detection and a graceful rebalance protocol. The fractional safety pool maintains a small, distributed reservation (expressed in fractional GPU-seconds and preallocated KV-cache space) across the cluster that can be lent to tenants during short bursts. A noise detector (lightweight EWMA + anomaly score) identifies sustained misbehavior at 30s–5m windows and triggers graduated mitigation rather than immediate hard preemption.

Key mechanisms: 
- Fractional safety pool: per-pool resource credit account (fractional GPU time, memory headroom) that is charged when a tenant exceeds its contractual throughput window. Pool refills on steady-state usage and via proactive autoscale events.
- Noise detector: telemetry uses GPU SM utilization, per-tenant queue depth, request size, per-token latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) and KV cache miss rates to compute an anomaly score. Detector parameters are tunable per-customer profile.
- Graceful rebalance: mitigation stages: 1) soft-shed new low-priority requests and route to lower-cost model variant; 2) throttle excess tokens for the offending tenant using token-bucket adjustments; 3) if persistent, move best-effort jobs to a preemptible lane or signal autoscaler to provision extra nodes (pre-warm) before hard eviction.
- Throughput guarantees: represent per-tenant contract as committed tokens/sec (CTS). Use an adaptive token-bucket reconciler that ties refill rate to observed steady demand and tail-latency SLAs.
- Quota enforcement: enforcement is a mix of soft (warnings, throttles, pool chargebacks) and hard (request rejection when pool exhausted and SLA breached). All enforcement actions are logged with rationale for audit.

Telemetry & metrics: per-tenant P50/P95/P99 latency, queue depth, GPU SM%, fractional-pool balance, anomaly-score, evicted_tasks, tokens_charged. Dashboards and alerting for SRE and customer success.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (simulation): batch-simulate noisy patterns against testbed cluster (two weeks).
- Phase 1 (dark-launch): enable detectors and collect telemetry without enforcement; show dashboards to SRE/PM.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable soft-shedding and pool charging for 5% of dedicated pools, monitor FPs and customer impact.
- Phase 3 (gradual rollout): expand to 50% then 100% with guardrails and automated rollback on regression.

Trade-offs & rationale: fractional pool reduces chance of hard preemption and keeps utilization high. Detector aims to minimize false positives (we accept slightly slower reaction times to keep FP <5%), but also must catch sustained misuse quickly to protect SLA. Graceful rebalance avoids moving live wallet-critical traffic unless strictly necessary.

Migration notes: expose new per-tenant contract fields in Console and API; provide migration script to map legacy quotas to CTS tokens/sec and a UI control to opt out of automatic mitigation for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Noise detector prototype runs in prod-data path with CPU overhead <=1% and computes anomaly score every 15s
Fractional safety pool accounting exists and shows per-pool balances in Console; pool balance charged/credited in end-to-end flow tests
Graceful rebalance implements three mitigation stages and can be toggled via feature flag
Integration test demonstrates throughput guarantees under synthetic noisy neighbor with <10% impact to committed-tenants and rollback path validated
Dashboards show per-tenant P95/P99 and anomaly rate; alerting for >0.5% of requests being soft-shed
False-positive rate of detection on historical trace replay <5% and false-negative rate acceptable within SLAs (documented)
PR merged with unit + integration tests and a migration script; rollout runbook documented in Confluence
Canary run for 2 weeks without >5% customer tickets related to degraded throughput
